_comment: Canon for every performance ratio quoted on the marketing site's high-traffic surfaces (homepage sections, page.tsx, layout.tsx metadata + JSON-LD). Same contract as commercial-terms.json: change this file first, then propagate. CI enforces it via tests/test_site_claims.py — a ratio on those surfaces that is not listed here fails the build. This exists because the site drifted: it carried a 65.6x figure attributed to three different repo sizes, a 63.6x typo of the same number, a 0.81s latency with no source in the repo, a '100% gold-file recall' that the current public benchmark contradicts (93.75% mean), and the real name of a private client whose field report the docs deliberately anonymize.

_evidence_levels.ci-gated: Recomputed and asserted on every PR. Cannot silently regress.
_evidence_levels.reproducible: Not a gate, but any reader can rerun it from a fresh clone and get the same number.
_evidence_levels.field-report: One repo, one developer, maintainer-measured. Reproducible in method, not in number. Must be labelled as such wherever it appears.
_evidence_levels.community: Submitted to docs/community-benchmarks.json by a named submitter. n is small; treat as directional.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: 93.75% gold-file recall (mean), 79-100% per repo, 90% found-rate, across 40 pre-registered queries on 4 pinned OSS repos
non_ratio_headline_claims.note: Do NOT round this to '100% recall'. Per-repo recall is 0.96 / 0.79 / 0.95 / 1.00; click is the weakest and every miss is published.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: Synapse recall lift +6.1 points top-k hit rate (77.2% -> 83.3%), budget-neutral
Faithfulness +0.143 expected-fact recall vs naive truncation at a matched token budget; grounding 1.00
TurboVec fact recall 0.800 vs chroma float32 0.744, identical top-k hit@4

unsourced_do_not_use.why: No measurement anywhere in the repo produces this number. There is per-query latency instrumentation (neuralmind/metrics_pipeline.py) but no committed benchmark result, so the figure cannot be defended. Speed claims must be mechanism-based ('a local index lookup, not another model call') until a latency benchmark is committed.
A transcription error for the 65.6x community submission. There is no 63.6x measurement.
Matches no repo in any dataset. 65.6x came from a 241-node repo; the 1,626-node repo measured 46.0x; the field report repo has ~9,300 nodes.

unsourced_do_not_use.claim: 100% gold-file recall on the public benchmark
unsourced_do_not_use.why: Contradicted by the current public benchmark: 0.96 on requests, 0.79 on click. The 100% figure came from an older, narrower competitor eval that the docs already flag as not re-verified against the expanded corpus.
